annotations.title: Bridge coverage: what cross-chain tracing covers

description: What ASPERN’s cross-chain tracing covers, exactly, and what it does not. Today a pilot: Circle CCTP V2, USDC, Base <-> Ethereum, one source transaction at a time on demand, with no history index and nothing stored. Not covered: CCTP V1, every other bridge (LI.FI, Wormhole, LayerZero, CCIP, native rollup bridges), other CCTP domains as destinations, volumes or market share, hooks after the mint, ownership, AI involvement or autonomy. With network and/or protocol, says whether that pair is inside the pilot; outside it, absence of a trace says nothing about activity there. FREE.

network.description: Optional: a network to ask about (base, ethereum, or any other name).

protocol.description: Optional: a protocol to ask about (cctp, cctp v2, wormhole …).

name: bridge_coverage

asked.description: The network and protocol asked about, null where not asked.

contracts.description: TokenMessengerV2, MessageTransmitterV2, TokenMinterV2, MessageV2 (same address on both networks).

inCoverage.description: Whether the asked pair is inside the pilot; null when nothing was asked.

meta.description: How current this answer is and what it was read from: `freshness` and the ages behind it. Present on every answer from this server, whatever the tool.

notClaimed.description: What no trace establishes: same owner, an AI agent, autonomy, same coins.

notCovered.description: What it does not read: other bridges, other domains, history, hooks, reorgs, ownership.

pilot.description: True: a pilot, not a product-wide index.

protocol.description: The one protocol traced: Circle CCTP V2.

rateLimit.description: Circle Iris’ published limit and how we stay under it.

sources.description: Where each step is read from: the two chains, Circle Iris v2, our vault flows.

statuses.description: The statuses a message can carry, only what the protocol evidences.

warnings.description: Anything the server wants a caller to know about THIS answer before acting on it. Empty is the normal case and is not a guarantee.
